facts.statement: The genus Janassa was first described by Schlotheim in 1820.
Janassa fossils date from the Lower Carboniferous to the Lopingian periods.
Five species are recognized within the genus Janassa, including the type species J. bituminosa.
facts.quote: subdivision: * J. bituminosa (Schlotheim, 1820) (type species) J. clavata M'Coy, 1855 J. kochi Nielsen, 1932 J. clarki Lund, 1989 J. unguicula (Eastman, 1903)

facts.statement: Janassa is known from teeth and poorly preserved body fossils found in the Kupferschiefer of Germany and the Marl Slate of England.
facts.quote: It is known from teeth and a few poorly preserved body fossils from Germany (Kupferschiefer, Upper Permian) and England (Marl Slate, Upper Permian)

facts.statement: The teeth of Janassa suggest it crushed and ate shellfish like brachiopods.
facts.quote: Its teeth suggest it crushed and ate shellfish, such as brachiopods

facts.statement: Janassa belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, the order Petalodontiformes, and the family Janassidae.
facts.quote: classis: Chondrichthyes ordo: Petalodontiformes† familia: Janassidae†

facts.statement: Janassa species had a body plan very similar to modern rays, with which they share no kinship.
facts.quote: Las especies de Janassa tenían un plan corporal muy similar a las actuales rayas con las que no guardan ningún parentesco

facts.statement: Based on tooth structure, Janassa is thought to have fed on shelled animals like brachiopods by crushing them.
facts.quote: Por la estructura de sus dientes se supone que se alimentaban de animales con concha, como los braquiópodos, a los cuales trituraban

facts.statement: Janassa lived from the Visean to the Wuchiapingian, between 346.7 and 254.14 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Visean to Wuchiapingian (346.7 to 254.14 million years ago)

facts.statement: Janassa is the parent group of the subfamily Janassinae and belongs to the family Janassidae.
